record.paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
record.original_question: For finite patterns, where a pattern is a word over variables such as alpha, beta, and gamma, and avoidability means that there exists an infinite word avoiding that pattern, what is the computational complexity of deciding whether a given pattern p is avoidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \{\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots\}$ be a countably infinite set of variables (letters of the pattern alphabet). A pattern is a finite nonempty word $p \in V^+$. Given a finite alphabet $\Sigma$, a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is said to encounter $p$ if there exist a nonerasing morphism $h \colon V^+ \to \Sigma^+$ and factors of $w$ such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$; otherwise $w$ avoids $p$. The pattern $p$ is called avoidable if there exist a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ and an infinite word $w \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ such that every factor of $w$ avoids $p$.

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem:

INPUT: a finite pattern $p \in V^+$.
QUESTION: is $p$ avoidable?

In particular, is this problem decidable, and if so, what is its precise complexity class?
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability and complexity of recognizing avoidable patterns over a free variable alphabet remains an open problem in combinatorics on words. Related variants have been studied: deciding avoidability of finite sets of partial words is NP-hard and lies in PSPACE, and deciding unavoidability of a single word (a special case) has been shown NP-complete. However, the general question of the exact computational complexity (and even a sharp upper bound for decidability beyond the known algorithmic characterizations of Bean–Ehrenfeucht–McNulty and Zimin) of pattern avoidability is still listed as open in recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: On the Complexity of Deciding Avoidability of Sets of Partial Words
status_evidence.snippet: Avoidability is NP-hard and in PSPACE; reduces to binary equal-length partial words.
status_evidence.claim: Related avoidability problems are NP-hard and in PSPACE, but exact complexity of pattern avoidability is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Complexity of Unavoidable Word Patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Determining whether a word is unavoidable is NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: Specific complexity bounds known for unavoidability variants, but general pattern avoidability complexity remains open.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Combinatorics on Partial Words (Blanchet-Sadri)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open problems in pattern avoidance including complexity questions.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of deciding avoidability is identified as an open problem.
